newsitem.title: LEBANON: British Bank celebrates 50 years in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: British Bank celebrates 50 years in Lebanon.

text.p: The British Bank of the Middle East celebrates 50 years in Lebanon on Thursday confident it has regained its competitive edge after the setbacks of the 1975-90 civil war.
Lebanon CEO Derek Kelly says British Bank, a member of the HSBC group, has invested more than $5 million in the past two and a half years to bring its services back up to international standards.
"We have been getting back into business in a big way, investing in branches, systems, people and products," Kelly told Reuters in an interview.
"We are now up to the standards we offer in other countries, having been quite a long way behind during those years."

One of British Bank's advantages is that it can offer technical systems and best practice from the global HSBC group elsewhere, while other local banks recovering from the war must develop their own, Kelly said.
Sir William Purves, Group Chairman of HSBC Holdings plc and Chairman of British Bank, will visit Beirut to mark Thursday's anniversary.

Kelly said the bank now offers some products and services that no other Lebanese bank has yet introduced, including the first linked network of ATMs and four fully on-line branches that enable customers to cash cheques easily at any of them.

"The job has been investing in our business properly to make up for all the investment we didn't do for 20 years, and starting to lend again and developing a will to win amongst our staff," Kelly said of his two and a half years in Beirut.
Memories of war have faded in Beirut amid the bustle of reconstruction, but for British Bank like the rest of Lebanon it has taken years to overcome the physical and psychological damage.

The bank pulled out expatriates during the war but it never closed because local staff carried on, sometimes running the operation from their homes. "But staff were shuttered down. They were on a survival basis until 1992," Kelly said.

On the personal banking side British Bank has launched personal loans, mortgages, Visa Gold card, Visa Classic card and an affiliates card for the American University of Beirut -- the first of its kind in Lebanon.
It has linked its Lebanon radio network, which brings the four branches on line, with HSBC's global network so that its global access cards can be used in Lebanon.
Kelly said the Lebanese banking sector is becoming increasingly competitive as many of the 82 commercial banks modernise and diversify like British Bank.
The bank has established two area office to support corporations, trade and industry where it can.
It is focussing on the import-export business and provides export credits for larger companies, Kelly said. It is also seeking sub-custodian business as the Beirut Stock Exchange develops.
Kelly is looking for project financing deals and when opportunities arise he brings in the group's regional investment bank in Dubai. "This is an area we are very keen on," he said.
He is also seeking industrial development business and hopes that industrial zones the government is developing will bring new opportunities.
